hints.title: Write the interior angle using the number of sides
hints.body: A regular polygon with n sides has interior angle 180(1−2/n) degrees. Substitute this and the corresponding m expression into the stated three-quarter relation.
hints.recap: The angle sum is 180(n−2), and equal angles divide that total by n.
hints.pitfall: A polygon must have at least three sides, even though the question calls n and m positive integers.
hints.pause: Cancel the common factor 180 and rearrange the relation.

recall.reminder: Translate the relation into an equation and simplify before counting cases.

hints.title: Bound the smaller side count before listing cases
hints.body: The relation simplifies to 8/n−6/m=1. Since m is positive, 8/n>1, so n<8. Together with n≥3, only n=3,4,5,6,7 need checking.
hints.recap: A positivity condition can turn an apparently infinite search into a finite list.
hints.pitfall: Counting arbitrary positive real solutions would ignore the integer side counts.
hints.pause: Express m in terms of n.

recall.reminder: Find a complete finite set of cases and check all of them.

hints.title: Check the bounded integer cases
hints.body: Use m=6n/(8−n), and calculate m for each n in the bounded list.
hints.recap: Both side counts must be integers at least three.
hints.pitfall: Positive fractions are not polygon side counts.
hints.pause: Complete the table, reject invalid pairs and count the survivors.

recall.reminder: Both side counts must be integers at least three.

solution:
180(1−2/n)=34180(1−2/m) simplifies to 8/n−6/m=1, hence m=6n/(8−n).

Because m>0, we need n<8; because these are polygons, n≥3. The possible n values are 3,4,5,6,7. They give m values 18/5,6,10,18,42 respectively.

The four valid pairs are (4,6), (5,10), (6,18), (7,42). Answer E.
